title: Post-install telemetry & hardening playbook — baremetal + vSphere
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic post-install playbook for on-prem Kubernetes clusters (baremetal and vSphere) focused on two things: 1) install and validate production telemetry (metrics, logs, traces) so we can observe and set SLOs quickly; 2) apply a prioritized set of security hardening measures that are compatible with our private-deploy constraints (air-gap possible, constrained network).

Scope and assumptions:
- Cluster provision is completed (control plane + worker nodes reachable from admin workstation).
- Provisioning may be via Terraform modules (vSphere or baremetal) but this doc focuses on post-provision steps.
- We target Kubernetes 1.25–1.27 (kubeadm-managed or equivalent).
- Minimal internet egress by default; references to images assume an internal registry mirror.

Goals (measurable):
- Install baseline metrics/exporters: node-exporter, kube-state-metrics, cAdvisor, kube-proxy metrics exposed to Prometheus within 15 minutes of playbook run.
- Logs pipeline: Fluent Bit forwarder -> internal log collector (Loki/EFK) with 24h retention by default.
- API audit logs enabled (at least control-plane write actions) and shipped to secure storage.
- Apply baseline PodSecurity/SecurityContext profiles and a set of network policies that prevent cross-namespace default talk.
- Ensure terraform state/backends and secrets are not leaked in logs.

Checklist (order-of-operations):
1) Validate cluster basics
   - kubectl get nodes -o wide  # verify node readiness and kubelet versions
   - kubectl get cs || true     # control plane components health

2) Confirm image registry access (mirror) and imagePullSecrets are in place
   - curl <internal-registry>/v2/_catalog
   - kubectl -n kube-system get secret reg-cred || create secret docker-registry reg-cred ...

3) Install metrics stack (manifest snippets below)
   - Deploy prometheus operator or kube-prometheus-stack chart from internal Helm repo
   - Ensure ServiceMonitors pick up: node-exporter, kube-state-metrics, kubelet (read-only port)
   - Verify targets in Prometheus: prometheus/api/v1/targets
   - Sanity check: curl -s http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/targets | jq .data.activeTargets | length

4) Node and kubelet telemetry
   - Deploy node-exporter as DaemonSet (hostProc/hostSysctl disabled by default for closed env)
   - cAdvisor is typically exposed by Kubelet; use kubelet service discovery. If cAdvisor disabled by distro, deploy cAdvisor as static pod.
   - kubelet flags to surface metrics: --read-only-port=10255 (deprecated) or configure kubelet-auth to allow kube-state-metrics scrape over secure port.

5) Logs: Fluent Bit/Forwarding
   - Deploy Fluent Bit DaemonSet configured to: read /var/log/containers/*.log, enrich with pod labels, drop terraform/state file paths from logs, and route to internal collector (HTTP/GRPC).
   - If air-gapped, push images to internal registry and update imagePullSecrets.

6) API audit logging (control plane)
   - Enable audit-policy with at least: metadata+write for core resources, requestBody for Pod exec/attach/portforward.
   - Ensure kube-apiserver flags: --audit-log-path=/var/log/kubernetes/audit.log --audit-policy-file=/etc/kubernetes/audit-policy.yaml
   - Sidecar shipper or cronjob to upload/rotate audit logs to secure object store; permissions limited to audit-role only.

7) Basic hardening (prioritized quick wins)
   - RBAC: Remove 'system:anonymous' wide clusterbindings; review clusterrolebinding list for overly permissive principals.
   - Pod Security: enforce restricted for kube-system? No — instead: default namespace -> baseline, infra namespaces -> restricted by label selectors.
   - Kubelet: enable authentication + authorization; restrict kubelet read/write endpoints.
   - Network Policies: create default-deny policies for non-infra namespaces, allow DNS/metrics egress to known IPs.
   - Secrets: ensure KMS integration or provider-backed secret encryption at rest (k8s encryptionConfig).
   - Admission controllers: enable NodeRestriction, PodNodeSelector (if using tenant partitioning), and RequestHeader for front proxy where applicable.

8) Terraform module notes / pitfalls observed
   - Keep state remote and locked (S3-compatible with Dynamo-style locking or Consul). Avoid local state in team-run workflows.
   - vSphere module: avoid hard-coded datastore names; prefer datacenter-scoped variables. Use template-based cloud-init to reduce per-VM changes.
   - Baremetal module: expose IP assignment as output variables (node_ip_list) and write to DNS upstream rather than inline-editing /etc/hosts in terraform.
   - Sensitive vars: do not echo terraform.tfstate in CI logs; set TF_LOG only when debugging and rotate state snapshots after.
   - Module convention: module.<cluster>.control_plane_count, module.<cluster>.worker_pool_names (list) — keep naming stable for later upgrades.

9) Upgrade plan (minor + patch updates)
   - Strategy: rolling upgrade with control-plane first (1 control-plane node at a time) then workers. For HA control plane maintain quorum (if 3+ control plane).
   - Pre-upgrade checks: confirm componentstatus, evictions disabled, cluster-autoscaler paused, node-problem-detector healthy.
   - Worker rotation: cordon -> drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -> wait for pods ready -> uncordon. Use PodDisruptionBudgets to prevent mass disruption.
   - Rollback: keep an image repository tag map and a short playbook to re-image node or revert kubeadm upgrade if a control-plane binary behaves incorrectly.

10) Post-upgrade validation
   - Run smoke tests: API server basic CRUD, controller-manager reachability, sample app traffic against service LB.
   - Confirm telemetry: no missing targets in Prometheus, logs pipeline shows no larger-than-normal gaps.

Quick commands and snippets (ops copy)
- kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m
- kubectl cordon <node>
- kubectl uncordon <node>
- kubectl get pods -A -o wide | grep Evicted || true
- kubectl top nodes | sort -k2 -nr

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we standardize on Loki vs EFK for logs in private-deploy? (tradeoffs: Loki lower disk but needs label hygiene).
- Decide retention tiers and SLO for audit logs (30d cold, 90d warm?) – needs legal review.
- Define canonical Terraform naming for vSphere folders to avoid drift across teams.
- Add an automated smoke-runner in CI that runs after terraform apply and posts to Slack channel #private-deploy.

References & artifacts to review:
- Internal audit policy draft: CONFS-4821
- Existing infra PR for internal registry: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/214
- Jira epic for private-deploy upgrades: JIRA-PRIVDEP-337

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic; aim for minimal blast radius for initial rollout.
- Please annotate items that cannot be automated due to customer-specific constraints (air-gap, FIPS-only crypto).
- I'll follow up with a short runbook for one-click rollback if we standardize on kubeadm upgrade path.

End-of-playbook (draft)
